To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Bursty Amplfy-Forward protocol is the optimal protocol in slow-fading relay channels at low SNR and low outage probability, and that it achieves the outage capacity.

in the low-SNR and low outage probability regimes, the outage capacity of a relay channel with slow fading is achieved by a simple amplify-and-forward protocol, and the outage capacity per energy unit is given by the sum of the outage capacities of the two direct links.
the outage capacity of a relay channel is achieved by a modified version of the Amplify-Forward scheme, which is optimal for low SNR and low outage probability.

the Bursty Amplified Forward (BAF) protocol achieves the outage capacity for the slow fading relay channels in the low SNR regime, without requiring any a priori channel information at the receivers, while the Decode and Forward (DF) protocol is suboptimal in that scenario.
the outage capacity of fading relay channels is achieved by the modified amplify-forward protocol in the low SNR regime.

the bursty AF is optimal for low-SNR and low-outage-probability regime and it is optimal in a sense that it achieves the outage capacity per-unit-energy of the fading relay channel in the low-SNR regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we showed how cooperation can be beneficial even when fading is strong, and we identified protocols that can exploit this cooperation.

we show that, at low SNR and outage probability, a simple amplify-and-forward scheme can be made to perform optimally by using a bursty transmission strategy, and that a simple decode-and-forward scheme performs sub-optimally.

the outage capacity of fading relay channels can be achieved in the low SNR regime using the bursty amplify-forward protocol, and this is achieved without a prior knowledge of the channel at the receivers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in low SNR regimes, the Amplify-Forward scheme is superior to the Decode-Forward scheme.
, while the Amplify-Forward scheme is suboptimal in the high SNR regime, in low SNR scenarios, it is optimal.
, in the low SNR and outage probability regime, the Amplify-Forward relay protocol with bursty relays is the optimal strategy for the relay channel.
